record.original_question: For generic holomorphic foliations on the complex projective plane P2, are generic leaves dense?

evidence.quote: In the field of holomorphic foliations, even in P2, the following are examples of open basic questions : Do leaves always cluster at singular points ? What is the topology of generic leaves ? Are leaves dense for generic foliations ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider singular holomorphic foliations by curves on the complex projective plane $\mathbb{P}^2$. Such a foliation $\mathcal{F}$ of degree $d \geq 2$ is given, in homogeneous coordinates, by a holomorphic vector field (or equivalently a section of a suitable twisted tangent bundle) whose zero set is a finite singular set $\mathrm{Sing}(\mathcal{F})$; on the complement $\mathbb{P}^2 \setminus \mathrm{Sing}(\mathcal{F})$, $\mathcal{F}$ defines a smooth one-dimensional holomorphic foliation, whose maximal connected immersed integral curves are called the leaves of $\mathcal{F}$. The space $\mathcal{F}_d$ of degree-$d$ foliations on $\mathbb{P}^2$ is naturally a Zariski-open subset of a complex projective space, and a property is said to hold for a generic foliation of degree $d$ if it holds on a countable intersection of dense open subsets (or, in stronger formulations, on a Zariski-open dense subset) of $\mathcal{F}_d$.

Question: Is it true that, for every degree $d \geq 2$, a generic foliation $\mathcal{F} \in \mathcal{F}_d$ has the property that every leaf (or, at least, every leaf outside a meager set of leaves) is dense in $\mathbb{P}^2$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether leaves are dense for generic holomorphic foliations on $\mathbb{P}^2$ is widely cited as an open basic problem in the theory of holomorphic foliations. Recent works (e.g., on unique ergodicity for foliations in $\mathbb{P}^2$ by Dinh–Sibony and collaborators, and ongoing studies of minimal exceptional sets) address related dynamical questions but do not resolve the density-of-generic-leaves problem in full generality.

status_evidence.title: Unique ergodicity for foliations in P^2 with an invariant curve
status_evidence.snippet: Unique ergodicity theorem for foliations in P^2 admitting an invariant projective line with hyperbolic singularities; results on convergence of leaves to the current of integration on the invariant line.
status_evidence.claim: Recent dynamical results address generic foliations on P^2 but do not settle whether leaves are dense for generic foliations in general.

status_evidence.title: Mathematisches Forschungsinstitut Oberwolfach Report No. 39/2017
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of open problems on the topology and dynamics of leaves of holomorphic foliations on P^2, including density and minimality questions.
status_evidence.claim: Density of generic leaves on P^2 is listed among open basic problems in the area.
